## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One test needs fixing: `test_rejects_legacy_header` passes because of the missing `END` line, not because of the version check it claims to guard. This review traced `parse_report` in `app/report.py` and checked all three tests in `tests/test_report.py` by reading them; it did not run them. The exact-match header check at `app/report.py:5` is correct. `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` is a real regression test for it: it fails under the old `startswith("REPORT ")` check and passes under the new one.

## Changes
`parse_report` now accepts only the exact header `REPORT v1` instead of any line starting with `REPORT `. The pull request also adds two tests that check unsupported headers are rejected.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:10 — tests — Make the legacy-header test reach the version check — `test_rejects_legacy_header` builds `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`, which still has a `v1` header and no `END` line, so `parse_report` returns `None` at the `lines[-1] != "END"` check on `app/report.py:3`. The version check on line 5 never runs. `rsplit("v1", 1)` replaces the last `v1`, which is in the body, so the comment on line 9 ("changing the fixture's version to v0") is also wrong: the header is unchanged. — This test passes whether or not the version check exists, so it gives no regression protection for the behavior it names and misleads anyone reading it about what is covered. — Fix: Use a complete report with a legacy header, such as `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"`, or delete this test, since `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already covers that input.
